why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository. `npm test` maps to the existing script `"test":"node --test"`, and that will pick up test/config.test.js. The files the briefs name all exist at this commit: src/config.js, src/app.js, test/config.test.js and README.md. The verifier's `node --input-type=module -e "import { loadConfig } from './src/config.js'; ... process.argv[1] ..." <tempfile>` is valid. With `-e`, the first extra argument is process.argv[1], and the relative import resolves from the repository root. The JavaScript inside the double quotes is valid and uses only single quotes, with no `$` or backticks. `node src/app.js <badfile>` and the temp file are placeholders the verifier fills in at run time. `npm install` only runs if there are dependencies. One small risk: package.json may not set a module type, but Node can import either module style here, so I found no command that would fail as written.
